analysis: Examined docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md head changes (line 3 date; new paragraph lines 670-689) and three submodule pointer bumps (libs/mlx 31f550a->72dffa2, libs/mlx-swift 4926d3d->c633d22, libs/mlx-swift-lm aee6ebb->2beb401). The doc describes a new scheduler partition (demandedLatestCheckpointRange, demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens = store floor, 64-token prompt-end margin) that ends a dense-Qwen prefill range at a deeper aligned boundary so the rolling-latest checkpoint sits closer to the prompt end. Per the doc, fleet-novel refusal, first/target/latest retention (max three), byte/count admission and storage floors are unchanged; this alters capture geometry only, not the T-041 controls (cacheSalt scoping, HMAC lookup tags, DBK3 AES-GCM/AAD, 30-min TTL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch). Checkpoints remain token-ID-bound in the encrypted manifest (line 808-809). Deeper latest checkpoints extend at-rest retained prefix coverage by up to ~4k tokens per donor and slightly sharpen the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035) granularity, which is within the accepted risk class; no new on-disk metadata is described. Submodule bumps carry the actual implementation (DemandedShortCheckpointRange.swift, EngineLoopV2, MLX core); source was not supplied, so correctness of the new partition (e.g., that it respects disarm/packed/preemption vetoes, retention caps, and that chunk-partition changes do not alter outputs for models other than dense Qwen per T-007/T-056) and any other security-relevant changes in the MLX/mlx-swift dependency updates cannot be verified here. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety; integration should confirm the gate is limited to dense Qwen paged complete store as documented and inspect the submodule diffs.
